bottleneck: NGRAM greedy correctness is BUG_CONFIRMED (canonical F1) and remains unresolved. The open fault-line split is (A) verify-row context misalignment vs (B) post-commit KV/bonus misalignment. The controller's stated open question is whether accepted draft rows [0,2,4] (identity retrieve_index, sparse accepted chain) are compacted correctly by move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache. This trial bounds that question on CPU before spending GPU slots.
hypothesis: H-CPU-1: the accept-index/KV-move arithmetic in move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache is algorithm-preserving for irregular NGRAM BFS topologies (including accepted rows [0,2,4] -> destinations [0,1,2]) conditional on the documented root convention that tree row 0 is the pending last token (spec_utils.py:606). H-CPU-2 (sensitivity/fault signature): if the tree root token is not the pending token, the always-accept-root rule commits target_predict[root] and moves the wrong token's KV into the pending slot, producing the exact off-argmax/behind-greedy signature reported for NGRAM. Both are tested on fixed CPU topologies with a deterministic target-model stand-in.
patch: No engine change. New pure-stdlib CPU oracle at ngram_oracle/topology_oracle.py plus raw results at ngram_oracle/results/topology_oracle.json. It ports reconstruct_indices_from_tree_mask_cpu (python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/spec.cpp:689), verify_tree_greedy_cpu (spec.cpp:249, matching the repo's _ref_verify_tree_greedy reference at test/registered/cpu/test_spec_kernels.py:204) and move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache (python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py:859: fill_front destinations + fill_accept compaction skipping -1 + pairwise move). Scenarios: chain, golden EXPECTED_BFS_MASKS[0] branch, sparse accept [0,2,4], and two fault-injection negatives (root != pending; destinations = accept_index instead of compacted front slots).
tests: Executed locally: python3 -I ngram_oracle/topology_oracle.py --out ngram_oracle/results/topology_oracle.json, exit 0. Result: chain PASS, bfs_branch PASS (accept [0,2,4,6,7]), sparse_accept_0_2_4 PASS (accept [0,2,4], committed == greedy, 0 KV mismatches), root_mismatch_NEG FAIL as expected (committed != greedy, 1 KV mismatch), no_compaction_NEG FAIL as expected (2 KV mismatches). all_expected=true, positive_scenarios_pass=true, negative_controls_detected=true. NOT requested: no GPU/fast gate (request_fast_gate=false) because no engine change exists to measure; a fast screen of the unchanged HEAD would not advance the fault line. NOT_TESTED: live overlap splicing (prev_tokens) and grammar no-splice branch; whether total_len == seq_len + 1 always holds at NGRAM draft prep is unmeasured.
learning: Bounded CPU negative finding: the KV mover's compaction is exact for sparse accepted chains [0,2,4] -> destinations [0,1,2] and the accept walk commits exactly the plain-greedy tokens on chain and BFS topologies when row 0 is the pending token. Sensitivity controls show (i) one mismatched root token immediately corrupts KV and the committed stream and (ii) omitting compaction produces KV mismatches, so the PASSes are not vacuous. Implication: do not re-open the mover/accept-index arithmetic as the F1 root cause; the live discriminator is whether the NGRAM draft path ever builds a tree whose row-0 token is not the pending token at seq_len (overlap prev_tokens splice, grammar no-splice branch, batch-composition changes). Limitations: pure-Python model of documented CPU kernels; CUDA kernels and the tvm_ffi corpus were not executed; target model is a deterministic context hash, not an LLM; no numeric quality or performance claim is made.
next_proposal: Cheapest decisive next step: add a host-side consistency counter in NGRAM draft prep (not a performance patch) that at each verify compares the corpus tree row-0 draft token against the last committed token that row 0 is supposed to encode (the pending token implied by seq_len) and logs/counts mismatches to server.log; run it on the existing batch-pinned ON/OFF repeat probe (512-token repeat prompts where divergence concentrates). Decision rule: any mismatch -> B-class corpus/overlap staging bug; zero mismatches with divergence reproduced -> A-class verify-row context (mask/positions/retrieve vs flat target_predict), then bisect the verify attention contract. Because this is an instrumentation-only change with no throughput claim, it should be bundled with the existing NGRAM correctness probe rather than consuming a fresh candidate slot. Do not gate NGRAM on speed until ALGORITHM_PRESERVING.
